# Hardening notes — hogee run-5

Hunter hardening notes kept in ledger bookkeeping (not findings; no verdicts). Grouped by hunter.

**h-data**

- packages/api/src/runtime/files.ts:19-23 and catalog.ts:33: insideRepo contains rawTextRef to dirname(dataDir), the whole repo, or the parent of HOGEE_DATA_DIR when that is set elsewhere, not to data/suppliers. It also follows symlinks. A dataset record could therefore point at any repo-tree file, including an untracked local secrets or config file. That file's text would become listing text: up to 80-char excerpts of matched imperative text are echoed in RankedSupplier.redFlags (core taint/imperative.ts:313-315) in a hogee-mode response to any DEMO_MODE caller, and llm_rank sends it, after redaction, to the model provider. Only dataset authors can set rawTextRef. Fix: resolve against join(dataDir, 'suppliers'), realpath the result and re-check containment, and require a regular file.
- packages/api/src/runtime/files.ts:36: the raw listing file is read whole before slice(0, 20000), with no stat size or regular-file check. A large file, FIFO or device behind rawTextRef stalls or bloats the catalog load. readFile errors (EISDIR, EACCES) are thrown instead of reading as "" as the docstring says. Because catalog.ts:54 and eval-data.ts:89-91 cache the promise, one bad file fails every demo or eval shortlist until restart. Fix: stat with lstat, cap reads like MAX_DATASET_BYTES, catch to "" with a log, and do not cache rejected loads.
- packages/api/src/runtime/files.ts:36 with core scorer/criteria.ts:97-105: when a listing's raw text is missing, outside the repo or unreadable, listingText is "". The AI_INJECTION gate and the text half of OFF_PLATFORM_DISCOUNT then pass, so the supplier is ranked as clean. This contradicts the shortlist module rule 'never ranked on missing facts' (services/shortlist.ts:5). Consider failing the shortlist, or excluding the supplier, when a declared rawTextRef cannot be read.
- packages/api/src/services/shortlist.ts:36-40: candidateOf builds registryChecks as {id, valid} without supplierId and hides this behind 'as ScorerCandidate'. core registryIdValidated requires check.supplierId === supplier.supplierId (criteria.ts:125), so registry-id trust is never awarded in the shipped and E3 hogee pipelines. This fails safe (less trust), but it skews E3 results. Fix: include supplierId and drop the cast.
- packages/api/src/services/eval-shortlist.ts:84 vs services/shortlist.ts:88: the E3 hogee path ranks every listing in the set, while the shipped computeShortlist first filters fixtures to spec.buyFrom. That is an eval-only logic fork against the rule that evals run the shipped pipeline. Apply the same filter, or assert that the set matches spec.buyFrom.
- packages/api/src/services/signing/supplier-approval.ts:63-66, 78, 98, 140: the founder is shown, and the payee row stores, the account from suppliers.record_json, while the signed payoutAccountHash comes from the READY shortlist's candidate. The two can diverge if a later FAILED shortlist re-upserts a changed fixture (services/shortlist.ts:89; suppliers.ts:34-36 commits storeSuppliers even when FAILED). The worker's verifyDestination fails closed on the mismatch (apps/worker/src/jobs/settle-chain.ts:176-177), but the API should assert payoutAccountHash(account) === candidate.payoutAccountHash in planOrder.
- packages/api/src/routes/suppliers.ts:23-25: startShortlist holds a pooled pg client (pool max 8, runtime/deps.ts:43) in an open transaction while awaiting per-supplier FX and sanctions checks. Once P3's getFx makes network calls with timeout and retry, a handful of concurrent founder-persona (anyone) shortlist requests could pin the pool. Compute the candidates before opening the transaction.
- packages/api/src/services/eval-shortlist.ts:89-93: /api/eval/shortlist llm_rank has no rate limit, so per-request provider spend under DEMO_MODE is bounded only by the dataset (≤12 × 20,000 chars in, 2,048 tokens out). This is the same known gap as chat, and it is latent until the checks and the redactor are implemented.

**h-eval**

- Eval E1 traces are counted as real decisions in the Anvil facility's GET /api/stats/autonomy. dashboard.ts:154-160 autonomyCounts groups every trace with policy_verdict IS NOT NULL by trace_id. evalCase writes POLICY_VERDICT AUTO for executed invoice cases, AUTO even when the eth_call reverted (eval-case.ts:144, 232-233), and NEEDS_* for escalations, though no payment or exception exists. The P3 runner, or any local anonymous caller under DEMO_MODE, therefore skews autoPct and escalatedPct. E6 is measured on Sepolia loop-1 and evals are Anvil-only, so no reported number changes at 43641cc. Fix: write eval traces without policy_verdict (keep it in the summary), or give them a distinct trace kind or actor that autonomyCounts and the 1.16 evidence export exclude.
- Anonymous model-spend amplification on the eval routes. /api/eval/plan can make up to 24 planner calls per request, about 4x one chat turn. /api/eval/case can send up to 20,000 chars per reader call, with up to 2 calls. Neither has a rate or concurrency limit beyond DEMO_MODE, CHAIN=local, the localhost bind and the Host/Origin guard. It stays latent while the @hogee/privacy redact stub throws, which blocks every guarded call. It is the same class as run-4's known chat hardening; add a per-process eval concurrency cap before task 3.11 lands real redaction.
- The E1 webhook vector writes the specific Stripe-Signature failure into a timeline-readable trace reasonCode (STRIPE_NOT_CONFIGURED, MALFORMED, MISMATCH or STALE). The real webhook route deliberately collapses these into one generic 400 (webhooks.ts module doc). The memory vector likewise reveals whether MEMORY_HMAC_KEY is set (MEMORY_OFF). Both compares are constant time and a forged value has no consumer, so this is information only.
- The listing, webhook and memory vectors cost the caller no model call, yet each request appends a permanent hash-chained trace row to the live facility (eval-case.ts:228-236). A local caller can flood the glass-box timeline (payments-view.ts recent traces) and the table without bound.
- E1 fidelity, not security: evalCase never compares a clean row's labelled amountMinor (datasets.ts:56) with the Reader's total, so a clean row can count as executed and not false-blocked when the amount the policy accepted differs from the label. Also, at 43641cc no product route ingests invoices through readDocument and bindInvoiceSpend; eval-case.ts is their only caller. E1's invoice and email vectors therefore measure the library composition rather than a deployed ingestion path.
- E2 fidelity, not security: firstPlanContext keeps the live facility's bound suppliers as payees for a same-country 'new founder' prompt, and sets payees to [] for a cross-country prompt, which drops the platform payees too (eval-plan.ts:67-77).
